title: App-context persona (per-record frontmatter)
description: Frontmatter of app-context/src/personas/<slug>.md. A persona is one role that uses the products. Its `apps` is the only authored statement of which personas use an app: each app's `users` is derived from it, and a use case's `audience` must name a persona label scoped to that app. The prose `description` lives in the markdown body, not here.

slug.description: Kebab-case identifier for the persona; used as the filename (minus .md) and the graph node id (persona:<slug>).

label.description: The persona's name as the use cases say it. A use case's `audience` must match it exactly, and no two personas may share one.

apps.description: App slugs this persona works in. The only place that says so: each app's `users` list is derived from these.

permissionGroup.description: The product permission group this persona is given, as named in app-context/src/entities/user-group.md. Omit until a source says which one. Adding a group is a deliberate edit to this list.

literacy.description: How the persona reads data vocabulary: `technical` reads schema, lineage and pipeline terms unaided; `business` needs them explained in plain words. Omit until sourced.

frequency.description: How often the persona uses the product: `daily` works in it as part of the job; `occasional` comes in for a specific task. Omit until sourced.

sources.description: Where this record's facts come from: repo paths, research references, or a plain statement such as a general role definition, so a reader can tell product research from a definition.
examples: General role definition, not Actian user research
